_comment: The budget has two tiers. Tier 1, EXACT: the per-file asset manifest and the artifact file count. These stay exact because they catch mechanical accidents rather than content: a regenerated crop, a re-subset font, a stray screenshot left in _site/ (that has happened twice), a file the build no longer emits. A file whose bytes moved is a file someone replaced; a count that moved is a file added or lost. Tier 2, CEILINGS: the document and the library. index_html_bytes, inline_js_bytes, library page_bytes and library index_bytes are generous ceilings rather than exact values, decided 2026-09-20: content moves every night this site is worked on, and an exact assertion on content forces a re-baseline into every commit, which stops being information and becomes a step. A ceiling at a round multiple of the current figure still catches the incidents the budget exists for: a generator gone wrong (a page set tripling overnight), a copy deck pasted twice, a script that doubles. Work under a ceiling ships without touching this file; work over one is a decision made on purpose, and the ceiling moves with its reason in the same commit. The gzip ceiling is a round 32 KiB against about 20.2 KiB measured: the compressor spread is around 50 B, so the ceiling carries many creative additions before it needs a decision of its own. History of every earlier re-baseline lives in git history on this file.

totals._note: The payload SITE_DESIGN_PLAN_V2.md §12.1 prints as 452 KB / 704 KB of exhibits. The plan's table is an estimate carried from the specification; these are the measured values, and on 2026-09-19 the plan's table was re-baselined to match them — the two are one commit. phone_1x is the 1x ASSET payload (exports + ground + the three fonts) and deliberately excludes the document, which is asserted separately under `document` below. RE-BASELINED AGAIN 2026-09-19, for the phone crops: phone_1x 194,064 to 237,991 (+43,927), retina_2x 388,356 to 500,885 (+112,529), and `exports_all_36` becomes `exports_all`, because the set is now 52 files rather than 36 and a key that counts is a key that lies if it keeps its old name. These are the sums of the files the artifact actually carries, recomputed by verify-budget.py rather than typed, and they rise because four exhibits gained a second, genuinely different crop — not because anything got heavier. THEY FALL on 2026-09-20 for the opposite reason: exhibit-12 retired, because act 4's exhibit is a live DOM replica now, so eight export files left the set (phone_1x -20,271, retina_2x -58,123, exports_all -185,174). The capture itself is not lost; its log was transcribed into the page, and make-exhibits.py records the line to restore if a bitmap is ever wanted again. A phone now requests the 600px crop in place of the 1200px one for those four, so what a device downloads falls while the set's total rises; the totals are an inventory, not a transfer size, and that was already true of phone_1x before today. THEY FALL AGAIN on 2026-09-21: exhibit-13 retired, act 5's dispute table now a DOM replica (the second exhibit to make that move), so four export files left the set (phone_1x -14,085, retina_2x -33,680, exports_all -130,225). The table was transcribed from the capture before the crop was dropped; make-exhibits.py records the line to restore.

document._note: Ceilings, not equalities. index_html_bytes_ceiling 131,072 = a round 128 KiB, re-baselined when M11 and M12 shipped together (78,643 before); still catches a doubling; index_html_gzip_ceiling is a round 32 KiB; inline_js_bytes_ceiling 20,480 = 20 KiB, re-baselined when M24 shipped (16,384 before, 16,856 measured): the close's cast release rides the scroll handler the wheel and parallax already pay for, and the reasoning above the block is the house's habit for code that could be got wrong twice. RE-BASELINED 2026-09-23: index_html_bytes_ceiling 131,072 to 163,840 (a round 160 KiB) and index_html_gzip_ceiling 32,768 to 40,960 (a round 40 KiB), for one direction the page is now openly on: the document carries its own generated art inline. The trigger that crossed the old line was real waste and was fixed rather than baselined - the rear-dials plates first shipped at 47.5KB of absolute float coordinates, and the house's own dashed-circle standard (355 holes in 1.7KB) shrank them to 19.0KB at 72 samples a turn, relative integer steps, visually identical; the document fell 176,146 to 147,822 B in the same commit as this re-baseline. What remains over the old line is the plates' honest size plus the M31 act label and M33 cold-state rules. The ceiling stays a doubling catch, not a target: 160 KiB over 147.8 KiB measured still fails any generator accident, and the next real jump is a decision made here, with its reason in this note.

library._note: The carried library. page_count stays exact: a missing page is a dead end for a reader. page_bytes and index_bytes are ceilings: page_bytes_ceiling 1,048,576 = 1 MiB over 633,110 B measured, index_bytes_ceiling 131,072 = 128 KiB over 34,635 B measured, so prose edits and generator output changes ship without a re-baseline and real accidents still fail. The shared files below stay exact: they are addressed by all 75 pages, so a regenerated theme.js or a recoloured stylesheet is a replacement, not a content edit. RE-BASELINED 2026-09-20, and the reason is a rendering fix rather than a design one: the stylesheet grew 50,980 to 55,112 B (+4,132) for four fallback faces and the measurement that chose them. They exist because the layout pass measured /what-is-a-local-llm/ at CLS 0.0395 with the fonts held 1,200ms, the capsule paragraph being five lines in the fallback and six in Inter, which moved the whole document under it by 27px. Nothing about the loaded page changes: the real faces stay first in every stack. RE-BASELINED 2026-09-21: /styles.css 56,514 to 58,263 B and /theme.js 3,924 to 7,665 B, both for one feature rather than two. The library's blocks now arrive on the landing's clock, so the stylesheet gained the marker rules and the script the fold test, the pace sample and the reasoning that chose it, which is most of those 3,741 B. The exact tier is kept rather than relaxed: these are still files all 75 pages address, and a swap of either for the landing's inlined copy is still a replacement rather than a content edit, which is the job this row does. RE-BASELINED 2026-09-21 again: 58,263 to 59,140 B, the seven group marks' one sizing rule. It is here rather than in a page because 75 carried pages and the directory all draw the same mark, and a rule copied into 75 pages is a rule that stops agreeing; the exact tier still does its job, since a stylesheet swapped for the landing's inlined copy is still a replacement. RE-BASELINED 2026-09-21, the search palette: /styles.css 59,140 to 67,222 B and a new row for /search.js at 14,371 B. The stylesheet gains the trigger that rides the header (seventy-five pages draw it, so its rule lives here for the same reason the group marks' does), the dialog's own type and grounds, and the measured numbers that chose the mark's colour: the accent under --cite-wash is 4.53:1 on the palette's ground and 4.36:1 on a hovered row, which is under the 4.5:1 bar, while the page's ink under the same wash is 15.15:1, so the marked word takes the ink. search_bytes_ceiling is the generator's own ceiling, stated once there and asserted here as a second route to the same fact: the file is fetched whole, lazily, the first time the palette opens. Nothing about a carried page's words moves: the 75 pages grew 29,250 B in total, one header trigger and one script tag each. RE-BASELINED 2026-09-21 inside the same goal: /search.js 14,371 to 14,732 B, a null guard around the count line. The audit built for the palette found it by doctoring the fetch to arrive early, which is a state a slow network reaches on its own: the promise resolved before the dialog existed and the whole success path threw, which the reader would have met as a failed load. The exact tier is kept, so this is visible as the one-line change it is. RE-BASELINED 2026-09-21, the fold: /search.js 14,732 to 24,327 B (+9,595). The palette's rule was a substring rule, which survives an inflection the page did not write and fails the direction a reader types most - "hallucinations" appears in no page while "hallucination" is a page's title. The script now folds a typed word into at most four spellings of it and runs the same all-words rule over the list. The bytes are mostly the reasoning: why each of the three families exists, what it was measured to buy before it was written, and why the two directions that naively look useful are absent. The exact tier is kept, and it did its job inside this goal: a row that appended instead of replacing turned "boundary" into "boundaryies", and the byte comparison is what made the change visible rather than silent. RE-BASELINED 2026-09-21, one rule in two searches: /search.js 22,728 to 25,236 B. The fold and the matcher moved above the palette and above its early return, because they are the library's rule rather than the dialog's, and the script now publishes `istorMatch` for the directory's own find field to call. The generated directory grew by the same hand (the inline script borrows the name and keeps its substring test as a fallback), which the index ceiling absorbs without a re-baseline. The exact tier is kept: this is the file every carried page addresses, so a change to it should be a line somebody looks at. RE-BASELINED 2026-09-21, one corpus as well as one rule: /search.js 24,327 to 25,236 B. The fetch and the parse moved into a memoized `index()` the script publishes as `istorIndex`, so the directory's own find field matches each page on the same text the dialog does instead of on its entry's title and summary alone - the difference between 1 entry and 9 pages for "parameters". The generated directory grew with it (a lazy read of that accessor plus the entry's own text as the fallback) and the index ceiling absorbed it: 41,370 B, no re-baseline there. The exact tier is kept for the file every carried page addresses. RE-BASELINED 2026-09-21, the temperature page's slider: /styles.css 67,945 to 70,301 B and a new row for /temperature-dial.js at 3,838 B. The stylesheet gains one component - the control's own type, its platform accent and the guard that keeps it off the printed sheet - and the script is the first file here that is NOT addressed by all 75 pages, which is not a reason to drop it out of the exact tier: it is still one file in one place, and a page that stops naming it ships a slider that cannot move, which is the failure verify-links.py now has a page-and-script check for.
